pairs.subject: combat-pacing-and-dramatic-arc
pairs.evidence: src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:956 The combat simulator API (route -> runCombatSimulationBatched -> detectAlerts) uses its own duration ceiling (60 s) and survival cut (0.3). The shared encounter-band law says stall at 45 s and brutal below 0.35, and the plain-language card calls a fight a slog at 30 s, so three sources disagree about one quantity in front of the designer.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:956 One global 60 s ceiling, coded inline. There is no envelope per encounter class, no floor for a player dying too fast (only the one-shot check), and no structural check of the effective-health ratio.

src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:1011 Restates a survival cut inline (0.3) that disagrees with SURVIVAL_BAND_CUTS.tough = 0.35 in src/lib/balance/encounter-bands.ts. That gives the band two authorities.

src/lib/combat/fight-report.ts:79 This is the technique's named failure: the narrated card calls a fight a slog at 30 s while the alert that gates it fires at 60 s. The thresholds are not read from one source.

src/types/combat-simulator.ts:143 The Monte Carlo summary aggregates survival, duration, damage and one-shot rate. It reports no beat rate across trials (no near-death, comeback or flat-pacing rate), even though many trials are run.

src/types/combat-simulator.ts:129 The fairness verdicts (one-shot, survival-low) come from a simulated stand-in for the player. A search for proxy/human/stand-in in the result types, engine and fight report found no driver-policy or 'human sample: none' declaration.
src/types/combat-simulator.ts:77 These are ARPG player-versus-enemy-pack encounters, with no laps, race or multi-entrant field.
src/types/combat-simulator.ts:86 A sandbox tuning slider for one scenario. There are no campaign divisions or tiers whose entrants would share a scalar.

pairs.subject: combat-pacing-and-dramatic-arc
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/gas-balance/balanceHealth.ts:495 The GAS balance health report leads with a composite A-F grade averaged from survival, duration, defense and consistency sub-scores. It never looks at what the fight does over time, so a squarely fair but flat fight is headlined as 'in great shape'.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/gas-balance/balanceHealth.ts:81 Bands named for actions (easy/fair/tough/brutal) come from the shared law, the numeric boundaries are written into the prose, and a separate win-margin finding exists. Minor gap: the card reads 'tough' as 'too punishing' rather than 'confirm the wall was intended'.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/gas-balance/balanceHealth.ts:147 One global set of cuts (instant <1 s, long >20 s, stall >45 s) applied to mean TTK. There is no envelope per encounter class, the floor sits well below the ~3 s 'no arc fits' floor, and there is no separate floor for a player dying too fast.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/gas-balance/balanceHealth.ts:99 Good: thresholds come from the shared law and suggestions are phrased as input moves. Missing: the sample size in the verdict line, a shape section that states absences, and counts out of ten except for the brutal band. The headline is a scalar grade, not the band.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/gas-balance/balanceHealth.ts:229 It guesses at missing near-death moments from the spread (coefficient of variation) of TTK instead of detecting beats. No near-death or comeback rate is ever measured, and a run with no low-variance trigger reports pacing as healthy.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/metrics/DroughtMetric.tsx:15 'Drought' here is a loot-drop interval, not the length of a fight.

pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/predictive/data.ts:67 The predictive simulator's heatmap and curves classify survival through private colour-only cuts (0.8 / 0.5) that are never stated as numbers and that disagree with the shared encounter-band law (0.9 / 0.6 / 0.35). The same survival rate is therefore green here and 'fair' or 'easy' elsewhere.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/predictive/data.ts:67 The technique names green/amber/red as a failure. Here the boundary exists only as a colour, the band has no action name, and the cuts are a second authority beside encounter-bands.ts.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/ResultsPanel.tsx:126 Duration is treated as one-sided, with shorter always better. There is no floor or ceiling envelope, and Avg TTK (predictive ResultsPanel) is shown without any bound.
